html: Cardiac rehab is a medically supervised program that helps people get stronger after a heart attack, heart surgery or certain heart conditions. A team of nurses, exercise specialists and dietitians tailors it to you.

image.caption: Sessions usually happen a few times a week over two to three months.
image.title: Illustration of a stethoscope

html:
• Exercise sessions with heart monitoring
  • Coaching on food, medicines and quitting tobacco
  • Help with stress and the emotions that can follow a heart event
People who complete rehab often feel more confident and have more energy, and they're less likely to end up back in the hospital. Ask your cardiologist for a referral.

title: Cardiac rehabilitation
abstract: How supervised exercise and coaching help people recover after a heart event.
